description: Work out which services an existing app runs on, from its files, a public GitHub repo, or its live website. From an AI coding app, read the project yourself and pass the files that say the most: package.json (or requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, Gemfile, go.mod, pubspec.yaml, Podfile), .env.example (names only, never secret values), and deploy configs (vercel.json, netlify.toml, fly.toml, render.yaml, .do/app.yaml, wrangler.toml, firebase.json, Dockerfile). Returns each catalogue vendor found with its evidence and confidence, services the catalogue can't price yet, frameworks and platforms. Rules only; nothing is stored. Then call audit_stack with the services (and their plans, if the user knows them).

repo.description: Public GitHub repo: owner/name or its github.com address.

text.description: Pasted text, e.g. a package.json or a list of services, when there are no file names.

url.description: The live website, to read its hosting headers and the scripts it loads.

name: detect_stack

assumptions.description: Usage and pricing assumptions behind the numbers.

caveats.description: Show to the user word for word.

data.description: The tool result. Its shape depends on the tool.

disclosures.description: Always includes the neutrality note: no vendor pays for a place in the answer. Link its url when you mention how Kong Reviews is paid.

title: Detect an existing app's stack
